newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Kimberly-Clark sees steady growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Kimberly-Clark sees steady growth.

text.p: Kimberly-Clark Corp expects to post steady sales volume growth for the rest of the decade and will boost earnings by buying up companies abroad, the company's chairman and chief executive said on Tuesday. Wayne R. Sanders told Reuters that net sales growth in 1997 would be "flattish" because of a string of recent divestitures of business groups, but volume sales by continuing businesses would increase by at least six percent.
"In our existing businesses, we are getting very good, steady volume growth and we expect it to stay steady," he said.

Volume sales growth of 6 to 8 percent per year in ongoing businesses and selective acquisitions should bring a doubling of earnings per share from operations by the year 2000 to $7.72 from $3.86 in 1995.
"There are a lot of companies that have traditionally forecast those kind of earnings, but there are very, very few that have delivered. We intend to deliver," he said.
The company earlier announced a two-for-one split of its common stock, increased its quarterly dividend to $0.48 from $0.46 and authorized the repurchase of 1.0 million shares of common stock.

The company also said it was getting out of the stand-alone pulp business by selling three mills in Ontario, Nova Scotia and Spain. Sanders said he expected to receive at least $600 million from those sales.

He said the divestitures would complete Kimberly-Clark's transition from a paper company to a consumer products company and would allow for higher-return investments in acquisitions and production growth elsewhere. Capital spending and regional acquisitions would total $1.1-$1.2 billion this year, he said.
Sanders said the company was now well placed for fast and steady growth, especially in developing countries.
